document.title: 'New Think': Our Long-Term Interests in Pakistan (Islamabad 06522)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] The embassy urges Washington to keep extensive aid flowing to secure long-term regional interests, since U.S. counterterrorism in Afghanistan depends on Pakistani support. It notes widespread Pakistani mistrust, "we helped you in Afghanistan twenty years ago, and then America walked away." It argues aid is the most effective tool for showing that the U.S. is a long-term partner.

events.description: Secretary of State told Musharraf the USG looked forward to an enhanced relationship including political, diplomatic and economic assistance.
President Bush reassured Musharraf in New York that the US would not let Pakistan down.
Ambassador Chamberlin cable to State proposing multi-year aid package (~USD 1.6 billion) for Pakistan.
President Bush reassured President Musharraf in New York that the US would not let Pakistan down.
The Secretary of State told Musharraf the US sought an enhanced relationship including multi-year economic assistance.
Ambassador Chamberlin cables Washington urging long-term multi-year aid to Pakistan (about USD 1.6 billion).
Afghan Defense Council vowed to continue anti-GOP protests despite Taliban reverses.
Ambassador Chamberlin transmits cable 'New Think' recommending sustained multi-year assistance to Pakistan.
U.S. agreement provides USD 600 million ESF budgetary/balance of payments support to Pakistan, with GOP to allocate rupee equivalent to local education and health.
USD 73 million in border control assistance provided as a kick-start for Pakistan's Afghan border security.
OPIC announces a USD 300 million line of credit for investment promotion in Pakistan.
Proposed EXIM visit to Pakistan early next year to flesh out opportunities.

key_claims: The embassy argues the US needs Pakistan's cooperation for counter-terrorism in Afghanistan and should reinforce it with multi-year foreign aid.
Pakistani opinion holds that America deserted Pakistan after the Afghan jihad twenty years earlier, and this mistrust runs high.
Taliban reversals and Musharraf's handling of extremists weakened the extremist element, but religious parties were chastened rather than disbanded.
Recommended package totals about USD 1.6 billion, covering development aid, budget support, border control, law enforcement, refugees and regional programs.
The embassy argues that muddling through as in the 1990s is unacceptable because Pakistan could again become a breeding ground for extremists.
Border security aid is meant to help Pakistan stop terrorists, contraband and narcotics crossing from Afghanistan.
